body.statement: Suppose randomized clusters are the units in \(I\), each has a prespecified finite scalar endpoint \(Y_i(d)\), and \(\mathscr G\) is fixed before the final assignment draw. Under the recorded conditional law, \(\Pr\{P_\delta(A)\le\alpha\mid\mathscr G\}\le\alpha\), and therefore \(\Pr\{P_\delta(A)\le\alpha\}\le\alpha\). The support and its probabilities remain unchanged across completions; no conditioning on survivors or on the selected row is permitted.
body.justification: The corollary turns a saved constrained allocation space into a valid prospective attrition-robust rank analysis.
body.gap: Yu et al.'s \(\texttt{cptest}\) uses residualized cluster-mean contrasts, and Hennessy et al. do not address missing-completion midranks.
body.consumer: A new \(\texttt{cvcrand}\) rank option can analyze a prespecified cluster endpoint while preserving the design actually used.
body.proof_tex:
Fix a value of the prespecified information \(\mathscr G\).  By the saved-support assumption, conditional on this value the sole final-stage randomness is the assignment \(A\), with exactly the recorded mass function \(w\) on the recorded fixed-count support \(\Omega\).  The cluster endpoint schedule and treatment-indexed observation schedule are fixed at this stage by the fixed-potential-outcomes and fixed-observation-schedule assumptions.  Under the sharp additive null, all hypotheses of the finite-sample-validity theorem therefore hold conditionally on \(\mathscr G\).  Applying that theorem to this conditional finite design gives
\[
\Pr\{P_\delta(A)\le\alpha\mid\mathscr G\}\le\alpha
\]
for every supported value of \(\mathscr G\).

Taking expectations and using the defining identity for conditional probability yields
\[
\Pr\{P_\delta(A)\le\alpha\}
=\mathbb E\!\left[
  \Pr\{P_\delta(A)\le\alpha\mid\mathscr G\}
 \right]
\le\alpha.
\]
The completion optimization changes only the missing coordinates of the completed sharp-null baseline vector.  Neither \(\Omega\) nor \(w\) is among its optimization variables.  Thus the argument keeps the saved support and probabilities fixed across completions and does not condition on the realized survivor set or on the selected assignment row.  This establishes the stated conditional and unconditional conclusions for the prespecified finite scalar cluster endpoints.
